tips.title: Precision Scribing with RB Productions Panel Line Scribing Tool
tips.text: Use RB Productions 300mm panel line scribing tool with a 0.2mm needle for fine lines. Hold the tool at 15° angle and scribe along the mold line with light pressure. For deeper lines, make two passes. Always sand with 400-grit paper afterward to remove burrs. This method works best on Tamiya and ICM injection-molded parts where panel lines are shallow.

tips.title: Photo-Etch Bending with Arma Hobby Jigs
tips.text: Arma Hobby photo-etch bending jigs use 1mm slots for precise alignment. Place the etched part in the jig, align with the slot, and bend gently using a 100g spring-loaded pliers. Apply light pressure for 2-3 seconds. This technique prevents kinking on delicate parts like ICM exhaust stacks and Eduard cockpit details.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Clear Solvent
tips.text: After each use, flush Iwata airbrushes with 100% Iwata Clear Solvent. Use a 1.5mm needle tip with 30psi air pressure. Clean the needle with a soft cloth, then run water through the system. Store the airbrush in a dry place with a desiccant packet to prevent clogging from Tamiya enamel residue.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya tape adheres better to glossy surfaces but can be difficult to remove. Apply with a Tamiya 100mm squeegee at 100g pressure. Kabuki tape is better for textured surfaces but requires a 2mm squeegee. Use Tamiya tape for decal placement on Arma Hobby plastic and Kabuki tape for weathering on ICM metal parts.

tips.title: Scratch-Building with Evergreen Styrene Sheet
